lead.headline: Iran and Qatar Keep Talking as Oil Prices Dip
lead.deck: Officials met for a third day in a row to look for a deal to end the war. Oil stayed expensive, but the price slipped.
body: Officials from Iran and Qatar sat down together on Sunday 1 November for a third day in a row. They were looking for a deal to end the war between Iran on one side and the United States and Israel on the other. Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araqchi, said the talks were “ongoing and progressing”.

Iran’s rulers celebrated the American midterm results as a rebuke of President Trump. Even so, Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei dismissed the idea of a major change in America’s policy toward Iran. The talks matter far beyond these countries, because of a narrow stretch of water.

That stretch is the Strait of Hormuz. Oil ships sail through it, and attacks on tankers there are raising energy and shipping costs worldwide. Brent crude, a widely quoted oil price, fell $1.59, or 1.40%, to $111.84 a barrel on Monday 2 November.

world.headline: Russian Strikes Hit Ukraine’s Power Stations
world.deck: Kyiv lost running water for more than 16 hours.
body: Zelensky said Russia hit power sites in four Ukrainian regions overnight, cutting electricity to hundreds of thousands of homes. Ukraine’s air force said it shot down 371 of 433 long-range drones launched since Saturday evening.

On Tuesday, Ukraine’s energy ministry said, Russia launched one of its largest attacks of the year on energy sites in 10 regions. In Kyiv, people lost running water for more than 16 hours; pumping stations restarted Wednesday afternoon.
